result: Plan written: head-first compare entry H2 (16-byte block at 0 before any size/ISA dispatch, ISA test after it) recommended; prototype head rows 11/1 vs Liella 21/4 instr/taken (glibc 13/2), Ivy Bridge __memcmpeq_head_128 1.75 -> 0.72 and eq_128 1.26 -> 0.70 of glibc; Skylake-family JCC-erratum uop-cache loss found in Liella's compare code; N100 timing pending

gate.affected: planning story: no product code changed; harness correctness check 4250610 checks / 0 failures

rulings.item: Extend NULL folding to every n for memcmp/bcmp/__memcmpeq (H2 loads offset 0 first, so NULL with n > 2048 gives SIGSEGV instead of the abort message)
AVX2 cost for the SSE2 gain: H2 adds one ISA test after the head block on n > 32 (about +1 instr on AVX2 eq rows, head rows -8)
Classed slot swap (D-4.53) for the compare family
rulings.recommendation: keep off; H2 needs no per-ISA entry

informational: Liella's compare code loses uop-cache delivery on a Skylake-family host (IDQ.MITE_UOPS 8-56 per call where glibc has about 0); padding removes it in the prototype
This harness's glibc memcmp is slower than in cbench, so memcmp ratios to glibc here are not comparable with the sweep; __memcmpeq ratios agree
A 3 s correctness check ran directly on the N100 host (outside its timing queue) while another story's timing job ran there
